derived_from.section: Work package W5 — Shadow policy and lifecycle reconciliation
derived_from.note: Refinement of the approved plan section into machine-readable criteria. No product scope is added, removed, or reinterpreted; every criterion traces to a plan line.

commit: feat(optimizer): default to shadow mode and reconcile stale lifecycle rows

prior_art_to_reuse_not_duplicate.org_proposal_recovery_service.ts: W1 package C already ships a bounded recovery sweep that ACTS: it re-projects lagging profiles and durably marks incoherent approved/applied claims. W5's reconciler is a distinct, strictly READ-ONLY classifier over ACTIVE scope rows for operator reporting. Do not merge the two and do not give the reconciler write powers.
prior_art_to_reuse_not_duplicate.markMeasuringUnresolvable: W1 package C already converts permanently-unprovable measuring rows to reconciliation-required. W5 step 10 covers the remaining case: rows that are legitimately RETRYABLE (telemetry unavailable, engine down) and today retry forever with no accounting.

criteria.plan_line: policy parser defaults to shadow, accepts only off | shadow | human_only | auto, and rejects invalid values to the safest mode
criteria.text: The parser is pure. Absent, empty, misspelled, wrong-case, or hostile values all resolve to shadow, never to auto. Only the four listed values are accepted.

criteria.plan_line: expose kill switches per change family
criteria.text: Each change family can be disabled independently, and a disabled family is refused at GENERATION/auto-apply time regardless of the global mode. A human-approved apply or revert is NOT affected by a kill switch — the plan preserves that path (W6 step 8).

criteria.plan_line: optimizer shadow run still audits/generates/ranks proposals but calls no apply, measure, revert, install, or target writer
criteria.text: A shadow run produces proposals and counters and leaves observable state byte-identical: all agent_configs rows, all agent_org_proposals statuses/revisions, and the projected profile files are unchanged after the run. Asserted as a full before/after state comparison, NOT by spying that a function was called (AGENTS.md forbids that form). The gate lives in the run loop, never inside applyProposal/measureProposal/revertProposal — those are shared with W1's human-approved route, which must keep working under every mode.

criteria.plan_line: preserving result counters that identify shadow candidates
criteria.text: A shadow run still reports what it WOULD have done, so the counters distinguish a shadow candidate from an absence of candidates.

criteria.plan_line: reconciler classifies active scope rows as effective, reintroduced/drifted, unsafe legacy rollback, conflicted, or unverifiable
criteria.text: Exactly those five classifications, decided from the current config and the versioned snapshot. A row that cannot be proven is unverifiable, never assumed effective.

criteria.plan_line: implement read-only reconciliation against current config and versioned snapshots
criteria.text: The reconciler performs no writes of any kind. Asserted by running it against a fixture and comparing a full before/after snapshot of both agent_configs and agent_org_proposals.

criteria.plan_line: operator script prints stable JSON and mutates nothing without --apply
criteria.text: Default invocation is dry-run, emits deterministic JSON, and changes nothing.

criteria.plan_line: --apply may only retire/supersede stale metadata; it must never restore/remove permissions automatically
criteria.text: With --apply the script may only mark proposal metadata retired/superseded. It must never write allowedMcpsJson, allowedSkillsJson, or corePermissionsJson. Asserted by comparing target scope bytes before and after an --apply run.

criteria.plan_line: measuring rows gain retry/deadline accounting or a deterministic inconclusive classification rather than indefinite silent retry
criteria.text: A measuring row that is retryable (telemetry unavailable, engine down) must not retry forever in silence. Implement the plan's SECOND option: a deterministic inconclusive classification derived from columns that already exist — no new schema, because W5 owns no migration file. Once a row is past its budget it classifies as inconclusive and inspectable.

criteria.plan_line: Reconciler reports the 69 legacy rows safely without changing config
criteria.text: Given the live-audit shape recorded in the plan (legacy whole-field snapshots on active rows), the reconciler classifies them as unsafe legacy rollback and changes no config.

criteria.plan_line: W5 acceptance 'Shadow mode has zero mutation side effects' + final gate 'Lifecycle drift is reportable with a default-dry-run reconciler'
criteria.text: The W1 recovery sweep must not become dead code under shadow-by-default. In shadow mode it runs report-only: it classifies and counts lagging projections and incoherent claims, and writes nothing. In human_only and auto it acts as it does today. A test proves both halves: shadow leaves state byte-identical while still reporting a non-zero count when drift exists.

criteria.plan_line: Campaign invariant: revision is the lifecycle CAS token
criteria.text: Neither the --apply metadata retirement nor the stuck-measurement classification may advance agent_org_proposals.revision for a fact that is not a domain change. The AFTER UPDATE auto-bump trigger means any raw update does exactly that, invalidating CAS tokens held in flight by approve/apply/revert/measure. Use a sidecar or an explicitly revision-preserving write.

acceptance_gates: Shadow mode has zero mutation side effects.
Reconciler reports the legacy rows safely without changing config.
Dry-run is the default and permission restoration/removal is never automated.
Stuck measuring work becomes inspectable/inconclusive instead of eternal.
explicitly_out_of_scope: Any automatic permission restoration or removal (plan: Deferred by design).
Requester-only canary enablement (plan: Deferred by design).
Consuming the outcome ledger — that is W6.

plan_interpretations.ambiguity: The plan never says what happens to W1 corrective-6's recovery sweep under shadow-by-default. runOrgOptimizer is its only production caller, so a naive shadow gate makes it permanently dead code.
plan_interpretations.reconciled_as: Two acceptance statements had to be satisfied at once: 'shadow has zero mutation side effects' (W5 acceptance) and 'Lifecycle drift is reportable with a default-dry-run reconciler' (final gate). Resolution: in shadow mode the recovery sweep runs in REPORT-ONLY form — it classifies and counts, and writes nothing. Its acting form runs in human_only and auto, where an operator has opted in. This keeps shadow mutation-free without making W1-C's repair unreachable by default. Encoded as W5-c11.
plan_interpretations.authority: W5 acceptance bullet 2 + final acceptance gate 'Lifecycle drift is reportable with a default-dry-run reconciler'

plan_interpretations.ambiguity: W5 step 10 offers 'retry/deadline accounting OR a deterministic inconclusive classification', but W5 owns no schema file and persisted accounting needs one.
plan_interpretations.reconciled_as: Take the plan's disjunction as written and implement the deterministic-classification branch, derived from columns that already exist (updated_at, revision, measure_reason). This keeps W4 and W5 genuinely parallel — persisted accounting would drag W5 into migrations.ts, postgres_bootstrap.ts and skill_schema_parity.test.ts, all W4-owned.
plan_interpretations.authority: plan W5 step 10 'or'; campaign dependency graph 'W4-W5 are parallel'

hazards: trg_agent_org_proposals_revision_autobump fires on ANY update of agent_org_proposals and advances the lifecycle CAS token — see W5-c12.
tsconfig sets rootDir/include to src only, so apps/api_server/scripts/ is NOT typechecked by npm run build. The script must import its logic from src/ so the build and tests actually cover it.
runOrgOptimizer is the only production caller of runRecoverySweep — see W5-c11 before gating anything.
